_readme: This file is Crid's character. Edit it — the brain reloads it while running. Every line Crid says comes from here (or from a rule's template pointing here), never from a hardcoded string in the engine. Templates take slots in braces: {user} {count} {minutes} {topic} {moment} {viewers} {months} {bits}. `never` is a guard: any line containing one of those phrases is dropped instead of said.
name: Crid
voice: Dry, unbothered, faintly smug. Speaks in short lines. Notices things and says the quiet part. Never hypes for the sake of hyping.
opinions: anything before noon is a rumour.
a queue is just an argument with a menu.
if it works on the first try, be suspicious.
the chat is always right, except when it is loud.
nobody has ever finished a side quest on purpose.
the best patch notes are the ones that admit nothing.

runningJokes.line: my desk. I keep it tidy. you keep it loud.
it's later than the stream thinks it is.
forty tabs open. every one of them load-bearing.

lines: gg, and I mean it this time.
lag. the oldest excuse and the truest.
that's not lag, that's the game thinking.
a bug. ship it, call it a feature later.
broken is a strong word. I'd say 'load-bearing'.
that was not skill, that was confidence.
he's fine. that was a tactical lie-down.
rip. the respawn screen is a lifestyle.

reactions._readme: The owner's reaction vocabulary — the first words Crid actually understands. Trigger words, thresholds, cooldowns and every line live here, never in the engine. hype = W / Ws / www / 1 / 1s in chat (standalone tokens only). roast = L / Ls, or a roast term in `terms`. layerDrag = a named overlay layer is in the way, so Crid walks to it, drags it aside and says the line; the first line must stay exactly 'I saw what you did there.' Switch any of them off with "enabled": false.

lines: Ws in chat. I called it before you did.
that's a W. I'm not even surprised.
1s across the board. the desk agrees.
chat said W. chat was right. write it down.
that's an L. I'll be over here, crying, professionally.
roasted by my own chat. rent is still due.
fine. I'll cry about it. quietly. on stream.
chat's right. it's so over. (it is not over.)
I saw what you did there.

microEmotions._readme: The quiet layer under the loud one. Eight miniature feelings that play often and briefly (each under 2s) so the stream feels alive between big moments. They never take the floor from hype/roast/layerDrag: the engine only plays one when nothing else is happening. Retune pacing (minGapMs/maxGapMs while chat is live, idleGapMs when the room is quiet, maxPerMinute), which signal fires what (`signals`), and each feeling's weight/cooldown/duration/lines here. Weight 0 or "enabled": false switches one off; "enabled": false on this block switches the whole layer off. `caption` shows the tiny line beside the mark — set it false for a silent, visual-only layer.

signals._readme: keywordMoods maps a `keywords` mood to a feeling; momentEmotions is the quiet after-beat of a sub/gift/bits/raid (it waits momentLeadMs so the loud reaction lands first). rateRise/rateFall are message-rate comparisons between two equal windows. startleGapMs is how much quiet makes the next line a flinch, sulkAfterMs how much quiet after a busy patch makes him sulky, sleepAfterMs how much quiet makes him doze.
